title: Embryonic neural stem/progenitor cells as model to characterize dystrophin and dystrophin-associated proteins expression during neuronal or astrocytic differentiation
author: Romo-Yáñez, Rodríguez-Martínez, et al.
materials: On the 14th day, pregnant female rats were sacrificed via decapitation and embryos E14 were isolated, washed and maintained in ice-cold Krebs buffer (NaCl 100 mM, KCl 2 mM, KH2PO4 600 nM, NaHCO3 12 mM, Glucose 7 mM, MgSO4 0.3%, BSA 0.3% and phenol red 0.1%, pH 7.4). The dorsal region of telencephalic vesicles was dissected with stereomicroscopic aid, and the isolation of the NSPC was performed as previously described [1], [2], [3]. Briefly, the tissue was mechanically dissociated in ice-cold Krebs buffer to a single cell suspension, and cells were recovered by centrifugation at 800–1000 x g for 3–5 min and were resuspended in N2 medium (DMEM/F12 1:1, supplemented with 25 mg/l human insulin, 30 nM sodium selenite, 100 μM putrescine, 20 nM progesterone and 100 mg/l Apotransferrin). Cells were seeded at 6 × 105 in 6-cm diameter culture dishes previously treated with 15 µg/ml poly-L-ornithine (Sigma), and 1 µg/ml human fibronectin (Invitrogen) in N2 medium or Neurocult medium (Stem cell technologies) containing 10 ng/ml FGF2 (Peprotech). FGF2 was added daily, and the medium was changed every other day. The initial plating was considered passage 0 (P0), and when cells reached 80% confluence, they were detached and re-plated to P1 and, subsequently, to P2 to obtain a homogeneous cell population. P2 cells were maintained for 4 days in the control (N2 medium + 10 ng/ml FGF2) and experimental conditions (N2 medium + 10 ng/ml FGF2 with 100 µM histamine or 10 ng/ml CNTF). Then, differentiation was induced by FGF2 withdrawal, in the presence of 200 µM ascorbic acid as an antioxidant to avoid cell death added every three days, and maintaining histamine or CNTF treatment, which was added daily.

Total RNA was extracted using TRIzol (Invitrogen). Six to eight micrograms of RNA, treated with RNase-free DNase1, was retro-transcribed into cDNA using random hexamers (Invitrogen) and M-MLV reverse transcriptase (Promega), according to the manufacturer's instructions. cDNAs were amplified by PCR in a 25 µl reaction volume containing 0.5 µg cDNA and specific primers (Table 1). The PCR conditions comprised an initial denaturation at 94 °C for 5 min, followed by 18–30 cycles at 94 °C for 30 s, 57–65 °C for 30 s and 72 °C for 60 s, and a final extension at 72 °C for 5 min. PCR products were visualized by electrophoresis on 1.5–2.0% agarose-TAE gels, stained with ethidium bromide and analyzed with Kodak Digital Science software (Kodak). steps.title: Sacrifice rats and isolate embryos
steps.instruction: On embryonic day 14, decapitate pregnant female rats, isolate E14 embryos, wash them and keep them in ice‑cold Krebs buffer (NaCl 100 mM, KCl 2 mM, KH₂PO₄ 600 nM, NaHCO₃ 12 mM, Glucose 7 mM, MgSO₄ 0.3 %, BSA 0.3 %, phenol red 0.1 %, pH 7.4).

steps.title: Dissect dorsal telencephalic vesicles
steps.instruction: Under a stereomicroscope, dissect the dorsal region of the telencephalic vesicles from each embryo.

steps.title: Dissociate tissue and collect cells
steps.instruction: Mechanically dissociate the dissected tissue in ice‑cold Krebs buffer to obtain a single‑cell suspension, centrifuge at 800–1000 × g for 3–5 min, and resuspend the pellet in N2 medium (DMEM/F12 1:1 supplemented with 25 mg l⁻¹ human insulin, 30 nM sodium selenite, 100 µM putrescine, 20 nM progesterone and 100 mg l⁻¹ Apotransferrin).

steps.title: Coat dishes and seed NSPC
steps.instruction: Treat 6‑cm culture dishes with 15 µg ml⁻¹ poly‑L‑ornithine (Sigma) and 1 µg ml⁻¹ human fibronectin (Invitrogen). Seed 6 × 10⁵ cells per dish in N2 medium or Neurocult medium containing 10 ng ml⁻¹ FGF2 (Peprotech); add FGF2 daily and change the medium every other day.

steps.title: Passage cells to obtain homogeneous population
steps.instruction: When cultures reach ~80 % confluence, detach the cells and re‑plate as passage 1 (P1); repeat the detachment and re‑plating once more to obtain passage 2 (P2) for a homogeneous NSPC population.

steps.title: Treat P2 cells and induce differentiation
steps.instruction: Maintain P2 cells for 4 days in (i) control medium (N2 + 10 ng ml⁻¹ FGF2) or (ii) experimental medium (N2 + 10 ng ml⁻¹ FGF2 + 100 µM histamine or 10 ng ml⁻¹ CNTF). Then withdraw FGF2 to induce differentiation, add 200 µM ascorbic acid every three days as an antioxidant, and continue daily histamine or CNTF treatment.

steps.title: Extract RNA and generate cDNA
steps.instruction: Extract total RNA from cells with TRIzol (Invitrogen). Use 6–8 µg RNA, treat with RNase‑free DNase I, and reverse‑transcribe into cDNA using random hexamers (Invitrogen) and M‑MLV reverse transcriptase (Promega) following the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Amplify cDNA by semi‑quantitative PCR
steps.instruction: Set up 25 µl PCR reactions containing 0.5 µg cDNA and the specific primers listed in Table 1. Run the thermal program: 94 °C 5 min; 18–30 cycles of 94 °C 30 s, 57–65 °C 30 s, 72 °C 60 s; final extension 72 °C 5 min. Separate products on 1.5–2.0 % agarose‑TAE gels, stain with ethidium bromide, and analyse with Kodak Digital Science software, choosing a cycle number within the linear amplification range.

steps.title: Prepare protein extracts for Western blot
steps.instruction: Lyse cells in extraction buffer (250 mM Tris, pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA, 1× complete protease inhibitor cocktail, Roche). Sonicate, determine protein concentration by absorbance at 280 nm or Bradford assay, and resuspend extracts in sample buffer (75 mM Tris‑HCl, 15 % SDS, 5 % β‑mercaptoethanol, 20 % glycerol, 0.001 % Bromophenol Blue).

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE, transfer, and immunoblot
steps.instruction: Load 40–60 µg protein per lane on 8 % or 10 % SDS‑PAGE gels, electrophorese, and electrotransfer proteins onto nitrocellulose membranes. Block membranes for 2 h with fat‑free milk solution. Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies: nestin (1:500), βIII‑tubulin (1:3000), GFAP (1:1500), and β‑actin (1:2000). Wash and incubate 1 h with peroxidase‑conjugated secondary antibodies (goat anti‑rabbit IgG or goat anti‑mouse IgG, 1:10 000, Molecular Probes). Detect bands using the Western Lightning ECL‑Plus system (Perkin‑Elmer). Antibodies H4 (1:5000), JAF (1:5000) and α1CT‑FP (1:1000) may also be used as described in the primary article.

steps.title: Fix cells and perform immunofluorescence
steps.instruction: Grow NSPC on coverslips pre‑coated with poly‑L‑ornithine and fibronectin. Fix cells with 4 % PFA for 2 min, then with 2 % PFA for an additional 20 min. Wash three times with PBS and block for 1 h with 10 % normal goat serum (NGS) in PBS. Incubate overnight at 4 °C with primary antibodies diluted in PBS + 10 % NGS: nestin pAb (1:1000), nestin mAb (1:100), βIII‑tubulin mAb (1:2000), H4 pAb (1:20), JAF pAb (1:20), dystroglycan mAb (1:20). (Additional antibodies used in the principal article: Sox2 mAb 1:200, MAP2 mAb 1:500, GFAP pAb 1:2000, GFAP mAb 1:500.) After washing, incubate 1 h with secondary antibodies: Alexa Fluor 488 anti‑mouse IgG and Alexa Fluor 594 anti‑rabbit IgG (both 1:200, Molecular Probes). Stain nuclei with DAPI (1 ng ml⁻¹), mount with Vectashield mounting medium, and proceed to imaging.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images and process
steps.instruction: Image stained samples on a Leica TCS‑SP8 confocal microscope, acquiring 10–15 optical z‑sections (0.4 µm thickness) per field. Select representative sections and analyse the images using Leica Application Suite AF software.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze data from three independent experiments with GraphPad Prism 5 using unpaired Student’s t‑tests; consider differences significant when P < 0.05.
